findings.description: A pytest setup failure caused by a missing fixture is accepted as an assertion failure. Pytest reports "fixture 'client' not found" and exits 1, but none of NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS matches that output.
findings.failure_mode: If the red commit contains a test requiring an unavailable fixture and green supplies that fixture, the script returns VERIFIED even though the red test never reached its assertion. The required red-before-green gate therefore approves a test that did not reproduce the bug.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject pytest setup failures, including missing fixtures, as NOT_A_RED. Add a regression case where red fails during fixture setup and green passes; require exit 4.

findings.description: The review role's allowed-tools list is a deliberate whitelist: only git diff/log and a few framework scripts are pre-approved, no test runner or general Bash. This diff adds `Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh *)` (and the matching hooks entry at lines 27-28). red-test-check.sh execs whatever argv follows `--` (cwd = a worktree, but absolute paths, network and the symlinked live node_modules/.venv are all reachable) and also execs the `--setup` argv. Phase 2 (line 219) tells the reviewer to take the command from the engineer-authored reviewer.md. The wrapper therefore pre-approves arbitrary command execution without a prompt, driven by text written by a different agent, which is exactly what the whitelist existed to prevent (unattended run mode makes this worse).
findings.failure_mode: A reviewer following the skill runs `red-test-check.sh --red <sha> -- <anything reviewer.md says>`; with the `*` pre-approval Claude Code never prompts, so a prompt-injected or careless engineer report can execute arbitrary commands under the review session's credentials.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not pre-approve with `*`. Either have red-test-check.sh read the test command from a tracked config value (e.g. a `test_command` key in .loa.config.yaml or the sprint plan) instead of argv and reject `--setup` when invoked from the review role, or restrict the pre-approval to fixed runner prefixes (`red-test-check.sh --red * -- bats *`, `... -- npm test`, etc.) and drop the wildcard.

findings.description: Both worktrees are prepared and both runs execute (lines 305-316) before any red-side verdict is examined (line 318 onward). A red run that times out, passes (DECOY) or fails to load (NOT_A_RED) still pays for the full green setup and run.
findings.failure_mode: A red TIMEOUT costs 2x --timeout (default 20 minutes) before exit 5; a DECOY or command-not-found red still runs the green suite for nothing, which matters inside run-mode cycles with their own timeouts.
findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate RED_TO / RED_EXIT / NOT_A_RED patterns immediately after the red run and call finish before preparing or running green; keep green's prepare after red's verdict.

findings.description: cleanup sends only SIGTERM to the run's process group, never waits and never follows with SIGKILL, then immediately runs `worktree remove --force`, `worktree prune` and `rm -rf "$SCRATCH"`. A test process that ignores or is slow on TERM is still writing while its cwd is deleted.
findings.failure_mode: On interrupt or a die2 during the second prepare, orphaned test processes survive the script, the scratch directory can be partially recreated after rm -rf, and `.git/worktrees/<name>` metadata may be left because remove failed while files were still being written.
findings.suggested_fix: After `kill -TERM`, poll `kill -0` for ~2s then `kill -KILL -- -$RUN_PID`, and `wait "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null` before remove_wt and rm -rf (the watcher already does TERM then KILL; reuse that logic).

findings.description: The gate is a hard calendar date (2026-10-13), not a template or framework-version marker. Any consumer sprint plan dated 2026-10-13 or later that was generated with the previous template (no Seams block) becomes a hard violation the moment the project pulls this release, with no migration path other than editing every sprint block. Conversely the check only requires one table row below the separator, so the untouched template placeholder row `| {interface the tests drive} | ... |` satisfies it.
findings.failure_mode: Projects that planned in the last week fail `validate-artifact.sh --type sprint` (and whatever gate calls it) on upgrade; projects that leave the placeholder pass with no real seam declared.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate on a plan marker (e.g. the template version in the header, or presence of any `### Seams Under Test` heading) rather than a date, or make the date-triggered path WARN for one release; additionally treat a row whose cells all start with `{` as missing.

findings.description: Sentence counting is `gsub(/[.!?]+[)"]*[[:space:]]/, ...)`, so every abbreviation followed by a space ("e.g. ", "i.e. ", "vs. ", "etc. ", "v1. ") counts as a sentence boundary. The limit is two, so one abbreviation in a genuine two-sentence definition is a hard violation, and the CI workflow runs this on the root GLOSSARY.md.
findings.failure_mode: A valid project glossary entry such as `**Foo**: The X used for Y, e.g. bars. Never for Z.` fails with 'has 3 sentences; at most two' and blocks the Glossary Terms workflow.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude common abbreviations before counting (strip `e\.g\.`, `i\.e\.`, `vs\.`, `etc\.`, `cf\.`) or require the character after the terminator to be an uppercase letter or end of string; add a GV case for `e.g.`.

findings.cross_file_justification: mount-submodule.sh (diff line 1278) extends the list of framework paths that are gitignored symlinks in a consumer repo (.claude/scripts, .claude/loa/*, settings.json, now GLOSSARY.md). red-test-check.sh (in diff) checks out detached worktrees, which contain neither these untracked symlinks nor the populated .loa submodule, yet reviewing-code/SKILL.md instructs reviewers in every mounted project to run it.
findings.description: In a submodule-mounted consumer project the worktree has an empty `.loa/` gitlink and none of the gitignored `.claude/scripts`, `.claude/hooks`, `.claude/settings.json` symlinks/copies. link_deps only mirrors node_modules/.venv/vendor/target/.tox. Any test that shells out to a framework script, hook or `.claude/loa` content fails with 'No such file' / 127 in both worktrees.
findings.failure_mode: The red run exits 127 and the script reports NOT_A_RED ('fix the test so it loads'), misdirecting the reviewer, even though the test is a legitimate red in the live tree.
findings.suggested_fix: Either run `git -C "$wt" submodule update --init --depth 1` (or `worktree add` with `--recurse-submodules` where supported) and recreate the manifest symlinks via symlink-manifest.sh in each worktree, or detect a `.gitmodules` / dangling `.claude/scripts` and emit an explicit 'framework not mounted in worktree' message with exit 2 instead of NOT_A_RED.

findings.description: The shape regex `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$` (line 82) drops every token containing ':', so the four `decision:*` glossary entries can never be matched and a misspelled kernel label like `decision:prototyping` is silently ignored rather than reported. Separately, add() (lines 127-129) registers `<name>s`, `<name>es` and the de-pluralised form for every term and alias, so an unrelated kernel token that happens to be a glossary word plus 's' (or minus 's') resolves as 'defined'.
findings.failure_mode: The gate reports PASS while a kernel label with a typo, or a code identifier that collides with a pluralised term, is undefined; coverage is weaker than the header claims.
findings.suggested_fix: Allow a single ':' in the kept-token shape (e.g. `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*(:[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)?$`) so label tokens are checked, and restrict the plural fold to exact `s`/`es` suffix pairs only when the base word is itself a term (do not add the singular of plural names unless explicitly aliased).
